The prose drafted on the back of these and several other related manuscript leaves includes ideas and phrases that resemble those used in "Unnamed Lands," a poem published first in the 1860 edition of Leaves of Grass.

body.head: Last littlesaved items from a vast batch ⁜left to oblivion. unprinted.
body.p: In its highest aspect, and striking its grandest average, essential Poetry expresses and goes along with essential Religion—has been and is more the adjunct, and more serviceable to that true religion (for of course there is a false one and plenty of it.) than all the priests and churches that now exist or have ever existed—Even while

Even while the temporary prevalent theory and practice of poetry is merely something ornamental and dainty⹀a love-sigh, a bit of jewelry, a feudal conceit, and ingenious tale or intellectual finesse, adjusted to the low calibre that will always sufficiently generally prevail (the ranges of stairs necessary to ascend the higher.)

The religious follies, crimes, banalicisms, aggregate and individual, so rife in history, are proofs of the radicialness and universally of this indestructible element of humanity's just as much as any, and are the other side of religion. Just as disease and proves health, and is the other side of it . . . . . The philosophy of Greece taught health and the beauty of life.
